sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: The purpose of this questionnaire is to collect key business scenarios and begin defining your future processes and configurations in your JAGGAER solution. We ask that you spend time completing this questionnaire to ensure preparedness for project kick-off, configuration working sessions, and a smooth transition of information to your JAGGAER Professional Services Implementation team.

sections.title: Portal Configuration
paragraphs: The portal configuration section of this questionnaire is intended to get you thinking about several system configuration decisions that will need to be made. The below sub-sections will introduce the system configuration decisions and provide guidance on collecting content and information.

sections.title: Branding
paragraphs: To provide your organization with the highest quality technology, JAGGAER will be branded to look and feel like your company website. The following items will be required to brand the JAGGAER instance:

Branding requirements will be reviewed during the Implementation Kick-Off. In the meantime, collect any of the above requirements or note below a plan to collect branding items (e.g., contact in marketing that will need to be engaged).

sections.title: User Roles
paragraphs: During implementation we will review all user right options (e.g., view only, edit, etc.) and define user roles (e.g., admin, buyer, contract manager). Prior to implementation, it is helpful to understand what types of users (e.g., buyers, contract managers, analyst, etc.) will be using the system and what capabilities will be required of them (e.g., build and edit RFPs, modify supplier information, etc.).
Please list all user types and their planned system usage below.

sections.title: Category Tree
paragraphs: JAGGAER highly recommends users to associate a category to each system object. A system object is any content created, edited and maintained within JAGGAER. System objects may be RFPs, RFIs, projects, auctions, contracts, suppliers, etc. depending on the client’s usage of the system. Suppliers will also select the categories they service or manufacture during the system registration process. Users will then be able to search for suppliers or objects within the system by category. Categories will be defined by the client organization and typically come from current purchasing or spend categorizations or standard commodity codes (e.g., NAICS, UNSPSC, etc.). Categories can be setup within JAGGAER in a tree format (a maximum of 4 levels is recommended).
Begin considering what categorization will be used for your category tree within JAGGAER. List below an initial plan to identify and finalize category tree to ready it for loading into JAGGAER.

sections.title: Business Divisions and Organizations
paragraphs: 1. Business organizations and divisions can be setup within JAGGAER and are primarily used for controlling visibility of objects (e.g., projects, RFPs, contracts, etc.).
Briefly describe how organizations, departments, divisions or groups are structured within your organization.

1. Is there a requirement to restrict visibility and/or collaboration of objects across your organizations, divisions, groups, or departments? For example, will a user associated with Division A be able to see system objects (e.g., RFPs, contracts, etc.) for department B? Please describe the required visibility and collaboration restrictions and requirements.

sections.title: JAGGAER Supplier Management+
paragraphs: The Supplier Management portion of this questionnaire is intended to gather information about how your organization manages suppliers today, and how you intend to manage suppliers leveraging JAGGAER in the future. The more we can learn about your business processes and requirements, the better we can tailor the JAGGAER configuration to meet your needs. Please answer as many of the following questions as you can with as much detail as possible. Keep in mind that the project team will be reviewing this document with you as part of the implementation process.

sections.title: Supplier Registration & On-Boarding
paragraphs: Supplier data management occurs through JAGGAER’s supplier registration and on-boarding process. The supplier registration and on-boarding process provides clients the ability to standardize collection, review, and management of supplier information while accounting for a client’s specific business requirements. A client’s business and process requirements will be incorporated into their Supplier Registration & On-Boarding module through leveraging various system capabilities and configurations. Below is a list of questions to allow JAGGAER to understand your business requirements for supplier data management.
1. Please describe how potential suppliers are registered (or potential supplier data is collected) today.
1. What data do you request from potential suppliers? (e.g. contact information, address, etc.)
1. How are suppliers invited to become potential suppliers with your organization? Self-invite and/or invitation only?
1. For suppliers that you want to do business with, describe how the supplier is on-boarded.

1. Is your onboarding process and data collection standard across all suppliers or does it vary based on certain factors (e.g., supplier category, supplier location, etc.)? Please describe any factors causing process variation and the data collected based on that factor.
1. What suppliers will be required to register on JAGGAER? What will be the intent of registering these suppliers (e.g., complete RFPs, manage supplier data, etc.)?
1. Do you check suppliers’ information against any third-party database? (e.g., OFAC, TIN, EGLS, D&B, etc.) If so, please list the third-party and describe the information verified.

1. Please describe any approval processes required prior to a supplier being fully registered or labeled a potential supplier. Does this approval process vary based on certain factors? If so, describe.
1. Please provide a current sample of your new supplier registration and on-boarding process within your organization. Provide any additional supplier data management information below.
1. How do you intend the supplier data management (registration and onboarding) process to change by implementing JAGGAER?

sections.title: Sourcing+
paragraphs: The Sourcing portion of this questionnaire is intended to gather information about how your organization executes Sourcing events. The more we can learn about your business processes and requirements, the better we can tailor JAGGAER configuration to meet your needs. Please answer as many of the following questions as well as you can with as much detail as possible. Keep in mind that the project team will be reviewing this document with you as part of the implementation process.

sections.title: Sourcing
paragraphs: The Sourcing module is used to efficiently create events, analyze bids and award to suppliers. We aim to create a consistent and repeatable process for buyers, which enables users to execute sourcing events and deliver cost savings to your organization.

1. Describe the steps in your current sourcing process (e.g. seven step sourcing process; ideation to completion). If you have any documents or process workflows that outline this process, please upload here. If you do not have a standard methodology defined, provide a general overview on how sourcing events are managed.
1. What is the throughput of sourcing events (e.g. RFIs/RFPs) executed on an annual basis by users?
1. What is the size of a standard bid – e.g.) how many line items and suppliers are included?
1. What is your standard methodology for analyzing and awarding supplier bids and pricing? Do you have any unique pricing requirements?
1. What are some of the biggest challenges your organization has faced with Sourcing technologies in the past?
1. What are your standard reporting requirements?
1. Do you have any sourcing requirements that you feel are unique to your company and should be taken into consideration by the JAGGAER project team?
1. Define success for your organization on the implementation of a sourcing tool.

sections.title: Auctions
paragraphs: The JA auction module enables the efficient creation, monitoring and analyzing of supplier bids. We aim to create a consistent and repeatable process for buyers, which enables users to execute auctions and deliver cost savings to your organization.
1. What is the volume of eAuctions your company manages in a given month or year?

1. Are there any auction requirements that you feel are unique to your company?

paragraphs: The purpose of this questionnaire is to collect key business requirements to help define your organization’s future process, and prepare for upcoming configuration decisions. We request that your team complete this questionnaire and share any questions, thoughts, ideas with the project team. Any open items can be discussed in future sessions.

1. If you will be providing lookup files, are you going to be providing a date range where the lookup value would be joined to your spend (see below example)?

On Feb 1 2014 Supplier XYZ is considered a small business. On Feb 1 2015 Supplier XYZ loses its small business status. The Client does not send the ‘small business’ supplier status on each transaction line; rather, the small business status is available on the diversity vendor lookup file that the client provides. If small business status is on the diversity vendor lookup file, two situations can occur, and we’d like to know if this type of situation is relevant to you:

1. If the small business status on the diversity vendor lookup file does not contain a date range, when that vendor file is updated in 2015, all of the 2014 transactions that used to show Supplier XYZ as small business will now lose that status.

2. If the small business status in the diversity vendor lookup file includes an applicability date range, logic can be written so that transactions with that supplier will be shown as small business or not small business according to the date range.
